title: The Truth Between Us
content:
“Tell me,” Lila repeated.

Darius set his keys on the counter.

“Vanessa and I ended our engagement six months ago. That part is true.”

“Then explain the photograph.”

“We attended a mutual friend's anniversary celebration two months ago. We had already separated, but we hadn't told everyone. It was complicated.”

“Complicated?”

“I know how it looks.”

“Then help me understand how it actually was.”

He took a breath.

“Vanessa wanted to reconcile. I went to the event because I didn't want to turn a friend's celebration into a public argument. We took photographs with everyone. That one doesn't tell the whole story.”

Lila searched his face.

“Why didn't you tell me about the event?”

“Because I knew you'd have questions, and I was afraid you'd think I wasn't ready to move on.”

“That's not your decision to make for me.”

“No,” he said quietly. “It isn't.”

The answer hung between them.

Lila wanted to be furious. Part of her was. But beneath the anger was a more painful realization: she had begun to imagine a future with a man she had known for barely a week.

She had let herself hope.

And hope, she was discovering, could make even a small uncertainty feel enormous.

“Did you tell Vanessa about me?”

“Yes.”

“Did she know you were serious?”

“I told her I was seeing someone I cared about.”

Lila looked away.

“You care about me?”

“Very much.”

“That's a big thing to say to someone you've known for a few days.”

“I know.”

“Then why say it?”

“Because it's true.”

She closed her eyes briefly.

Darius moved closer, then stopped when she raised her hand.

“Please. I need a little space.”

He nodded.

“All right.”

She had expected him to argue, to plead, or to try to charm his way out of the situation. Instead, he respected her request.

That somehow made everything harder.

At the door, he turned back.

“I should have told you everything from the beginning. I'm sorry.”

Lila said nothing.

“I won't pressure you to forgive me. But if you decide you want to talk, I'll be here.”

Then he left.

For two days, the house next door remained painfully quiet.

Lila went to work, answered emails, and pretended she wasn't listening for the sound of Darius's car. She told herself she was being sensible. She reminded herself that attraction wasn't a reason to ignore her boundaries.

But she also missed him.

She missed the way he remembered her coffee. The way he made her laugh when she was trying to be serious. The way conversation with him could move from ridiculous jokes to honest confessions without feeling forced.

Most of all, she missed the possibility that something good might come from their unexpected meeting.

On Wednesday evening, she found a small envelope tucked beneath her door.

Inside was a handwritten note.

Lila,

You don't owe me another chance. I only want you to know that meeting you wasn't part of some plan to escape my past. I moved because I needed a fresh start. I didn't expect to meet you, and I certainly didn't expect to care about you this quickly.

I should have trusted you enough to tell you the truth before you had to ask.

I'm sorry.

— Darius

She read it twice.

Then she walked to the front window.

Darius was outside, carrying a box into his house. He glanced toward her window but didn't wave.

He wasn't trying to force a conversation.

He was giving her the choice.

Lila stood there for another minute before grabbing her keys.

She crossed the lawn and knocked on his door.

When he opened it, surprise flashed across his face.

“Lila.”

“I'm still angry with you.”

“I understand.”

“And I don't want to be involved in unfinished business with your ex.”

“You won't be.”

“I need honesty, even when it's uncomfortable.”

“You have my word.”

She studied him.

“Words are easy, Darius.”

“I know. I'll have to prove it.”

For a moment, neither moved.

Then Lila stepped closer.

“I missed you.”

His expression softened.

“I missed you too.”

She reached for his hand.

“This doesn't mean everything is magically fixed.”

“I wouldn't expect that.”

“And if you ever hide something important from me again—”

“I know.”

“No, let me finish.”

He smiled faintly.

“I'm listening.”

She shook her head, fighting a smile of her own.

“You're impossible.”

“Occasionally.”

She looked up at him, and the familiar warmth between them began to return—not as a replacement for the difficult conversation, but as something that could exist alongside it.

“Can I kiss you?” he asked.

Lila pretended to consider the question.

“I'm not sure you've earned it.”

“Then I'll wait.”

She smiled.

That was what decided it.

She closed the distance herself and kissed him, slowly at first, then with the unmistakable affection she'd been trying to suppress for two days.

When they parted, Darius rested his forehead against hers.

“Does this mean I can take you to dinner again?”

“It means you can ask.”

“Saturday?”

“Maybe.”

“Eight o'clock?”

“Bring flowers.”

He laughed.

“Anything else?”

She pretended to think.

“Don't make me regret this.”

His expression grew serious.

“I won't take your trust for granted again.”

She believed he meant it.

Whether he would prove it was something only time could answer.

Lila took his hand, and together they stepped out onto the porch. The evening air was cool, the street peaceful, and the lights in the neighboring houses glowed against the gathering dusk.

For the first time, she understood that the real danger of the tall, dark neighbor wasn't how easily he could make her heart race.

It was how easily he could make her want to trust again.

And as Darius turned toward her with that familiar, irresistible smile, Lila knew one thing for certain.

Their story was nowhere near finished.
